newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: INTERVIEW - Portugal/Germany bond spread too wide.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Portugal/Germany bond spread too wide.

text.p: Widened spreads between the Portuguese and German bond markets do not reflect economic realities and will narrow again once markets realise that Portugal will enter the European single currency, Portugal's deputy finance minister said.

Fernando Teixeira dos Santos told Reuters that spreads close to 80 basis points for the benchmark 10-year cash bond, levels reached last January when optimism over the single currency was at its height, were more appropriate than current rates.
The spread stood at 135 basis points on Tuesday.

Teixeira dos Santos said in an interview on Monday night that the sudden widening of the spreads was due to unfounded fears of a delay in the launching of economic and monetary union (EMU) and concerns that southern European countries, including Portugal, might not be included in the first wave.
"Taking account of the fundamentals of the Portuguese economy, it is my opinion that this spread (in January) reflects more accurately the real economic situation than the current spreads," he said.

Teixeira dos Santos said that comments about southern Europe possibly being excluded from monetary union rarely mentioned Portugal individually but the country was somehow lumped together with Spain and Italy.
"They are generic statements that question the capacity of some countries to enter monetary union and which do not refer specifically to Portugal," he said.

Teixeira dos Santos said that he was convinced this "noise" -- as he called recent statements questioning southern Europe's credentials -- would only have a temporary impact and that Portuguese bonds would recover as markets became convinced again that the country would qualify for monetary union.
"The markets are not wrong. The people who have got it wrong are those that introduce these doubts," he said.
